name: Geert Wilders
role: Dutch member of parliament and founder of the Party for Freedom (PVV)
summary: Wilders advocates sharply restricting immigration and restricting Islamic institutions and practices in the Netherlands. He emphasizes Dutch sovereignty and cultural identity, and has called for directing public spending toward Dutch households and services.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: In section 5 he proposes retaining the armed forces and giving them a role in maintaining public order when necessary.

abolish-ip.rationale: In section 2 he advocates extending patent protection as part of his plan to stimulate innovation.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: In section 5 Wilders calls for a substantial increase in the number of police officers and for police stations throughout the country to be open around the clock.

apologise-for-past-wrongs.rationale: Wilders explicitly rejects calls for the Dutch government to apologize for its role in slavery.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: In defending his bill, Wilders condemned punishing people with death for leaving Islam and described the freedom to leave it as a right that should be protected.

common-currency.rationale: Wilders describes the euro as doing more harm than good and calls for the Netherlands to regain control over its own money.

consent-of-governed.rationale: In section 10 he invokes the Dutch repudiation of a sovereign who treated the people as existing for him and proposes giving citizens more direct control over their representatives.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: In section 2 he calls for dismantling the Dutch corporatist consultation system and ending the general extension of collective agreements.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Wilders explicitly describes Western culture as superior to Islamic culture and rejects cultural relativism.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: Wilders filed a motion to eliminate VAT on groceries.

direct-votes.rationale: Wilders voted for both constitutional proposals in the 5 July 2022 roll calls on a binding corrective referendum, which would let voters reject legislation.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Wilders condemns spending billions on climate policy and calls for redirecting those funds to Dutch households.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Wilders explicitly calls for preserving NATO as the transatlantic organization he considers responsible for Dutch security.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Wilders and De Graaf introduced a bill that would deny Islamic institutions and practices legal protections available to other religious communities.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Wilders advocated investment to speed up North Sea gas extraction and said he would support extraction in Groningen if local voters backed it and residents were compensated.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Wilders told the House he would support a plan to build ten nuclear stations in the Netherlands, citing France’s long-term investment in nuclear generation.

flat-income-tax.rationale: In section 2 he calls for tax reductions to culminate in a flat tax.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: In section 7 he explicitly proposes abolishing municipal voting rights for residents without Dutch nationality.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Wilders argues that Islamic doctrine conflicts with the rights and freedoms protected by the Dutch democratic state.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Wilders explicitly defends Israel as the national home of the Jewish people.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: In section 7 he proposes making ten years of legal employment in the Netherlands a condition for naturalization.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: In section 5 he proposes mandatory minimums and a life sentence after three violent offenses.

nation-first.rationale: In his signed foreword Wilders says Dutch public money should go to the purchasing power and well-being of Dutch people, and objects to spending it on Brussels and foreign aid instead.

night-watchman-state.rationale: In section 2 he assigns the state responsibility for a reliable social safety net for people who are sick or unable to find work.

open-borders.rationale: Wilders submitted motion 36800 no. 5 calling for substantially stronger national border controls under Article 72 of the EU treaty.

party-controls-media.rationale: In section 10 he explicitly calls for independent, plural media.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: In section 10 he characterizes parliamentarians as preoccupied with their own interests and describes established parties distributing desirable public posts among themselves.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Wilders explicitly calls for the Netherlands to leave the European Union, citing the loss of national democratic control to Brussels.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Wilders calls on Europeans to defend their inherited traditions and national identity, which he describes as under threat.

private-courts-defense.rationale: In section 10 he proposes changing the selection of public court members to direct election and introducing jury trials.

public-service-media.rationale: In section 10 he proposes retaining a public television channel for the NOS as part of an independent, plural media system.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: In chapter 1 Wilders defends the right to publish depictions of Muhammad and criticizes treating such depictions as offenses.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Wilders co-signed motion 60 asking the Dutch government to identify the mass killing of Armenians as genocide in relevant official statements.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Wilders filed motion 36760 no. 25 calling for a complete asylum stop, an end to family reunification and much stricter border checks.

rehabilitation.rationale: In section 5 he puts punishment and victims ahead of efforts to help convicted offenders reestablish their lives, and calls for more austere imprisonment.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Wilders explicitly defends the freedom to change religions and to leave Islam.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: In section 7 he proposes prohibiting finance for religious organizations from foreign extremist groups, naming examples from Morocco and Saudi Arabia.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: In section 9 of his 2005 declaration, Wilders urged stronger prosecution of incitement to hatred. In Copenhagen he called for repealing European hate-speech laws.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Wilders co-sponsored motion 36800 XVII no. 34 calling for an immediate end to all forms of Dutch development aid.

second-chamber.rationale: In section 10 he proposes abolishing the Senate and transferring its reviewing function to the Council of State.

separate-church-state.rationale: In the signed op-ed Wilders explicitly names separation of church and state as a feature of Dutch and European society that he wants to preserve.

separated-powers.rationale: Wilders criticizes what he describes as the loss of separation between the cabinet, prosecutors and judges, arguing that the judiciary should have independence from the executive.

social-market-economy.rationale: In section 2 he advocates a private-enterprise economy coupled with a government safety net for people who are sick or cannot find work.

state-harmful.rationale: He calls for keeping government and relying on a strong state where its responsibilities require one.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: His proposal in section 2 calls for a flat income tax in place of graduated rates.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: In section 7 he states that access to social security should begin only once a person acquires Dutch nationality.

work-for-welfare.rationale: In section 2 he would require recipients who are able to work to perform community work in exchange for benefits until they find regular work.

notes: Research covered economy and welfare, government and electoral rules, society and culture, foreign affairs and global institutions, civil liberties, ecology and energy, technology, and methods of political change. It used the 2005 declaration, the signed 2025 foreword, speeches, the ParlaMint Netherlands corpus as a lead to official Dutch transcripts, and parliamentary motions and bills. The Everand excerpt contains part of chapter 1 of Marked for Death.
